text: This year, Portland Public Schools
serves more than 40,000 students at 81
schools with an operating budget of
about $868 million. You may wonder,
where does that money come from? Most of
it, what we call the general fund, comes
from the state school fund. That's a mix
of state income taxes and local property
taxes, which are shared across Oregon
districts through something called the
equalization formula. This formula means
the amount of money we receive depends
on the number of students we serve. When
enrollment goes up, funding goes up.
When enrollment goes down, funding also
goes down. And like many districts, PPS
has seen a steady enrollment decline in
recent years. That decline, combined
with rising costs, is one of the biggest
reasons for our budget challenges.
Portlanders are also support PPS through
the local option levy, a voter-approved
property tax that provides additional
revenue. But even that levy has been
squeezed lately because of declining
property values. Put simply, costs are
rising faster than our income.
Understanding this dynamic is the first
step to understanding our budget.
